name: Honda CB350 / CL350
engine: 325 cc air-cooled SOHC parallel twin, two carbs
intro: A very common first restoration, with a big owner community and good parts supply.

H-001.title: Change the oil and clean the oil slinger
H-001.instructions: Drain the oil, then take off the right-hand cover and clean out the centrifugal oil filter (the oil slinger). Look at what's inside it before you clean it.
H-001.reason: This engine has no paper filter. Sludge and bits of a broken cam chain roller collect in the slinger.

add.title: Check the cam chain tensioner roller
add.instructions: Inspect the cam chain tensioner roller. The original was rubber and goes hard and brittle with age. Bits in the oil slinger mean it's breaking up.
add.reason: A failing roller lets the cam chain slap and sends debris through the engine.

add.title: Check the points-side cam bearing
add.instructions: Before setting the points, check the cam bearing cover on the points side for wear and oil weeping.
add.reason: A worn cam bearing lets the points gap and timing wander even after you set them.

L: Don't overtighten the drive chain. Owners see that often on these bikes.

recallNote: Any recalls on bikes this old were closed long ago.

known.title: Cam chain tensioner roller
known.what: The rubber roller goes brittle and breaks up.

known.title: Points timing wanders
known.what: A worn points-side cam bearing changes the gap.

known.title: Overtight chain
known.what: Owners often run the drive chain too tight.
